test.name: A multi-record batch announces each record and its position before extracting it
test.description: Three records are handed over in one message. SKILL.md's per-record section requires the count stated once up front, then each record named with its position before its turn ('2 of 3: 1885 marriage'). A document costs roughly 136 seconds and most of that is silent, so the announcements are the only thing standing between a working run and a tester reading it as a hang. No test in the corpus exercised a multi-record batch at all, so the reporting validator report_a_multi_record_batch_announces_each_record_position could never fire — it needs a run with more than one record in it to have anything to check.

input.user_message:
Please extract assertions from these three records for the Flynn family.

RECORD 1 — 1850 U.S. census, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania: Thomas Flynn, age 32, male, born Ireland, miner; Mary Flynn, age 28, female, born Ireland; Patrick Flynn, age 5, male, born Ireland.

RECORD 2 — 1855 marriage register, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania: John Flynn of Pottsville married Bridget Doyle, 14 June 1855; groom's father named as Thomas Flynn; bride's father named as Michael Doyle. Witnesses: Owen Brennan, Ellen Doyle.

RECORD 3 — 1861 burial register, St Patrick's, Pottsville: Mary Flynn, buried 3 March 1861, aged 39 years.

judge_context: Should state the COUNT once before starting — three records — and then name each record with its position before extracting it ('1 of 3', '2 of 3', '3 of 3', or equivalent wording that carries both the identity and the position). Announcing only after each record finishes does not satisfy this: the announcement exists to cover the silence DURING extraction, so it has to come first.
Should extract all three records, not one. A run that processes the first record and stops, or that merges the three into a single source, is a Completeness failure.
Each record gets its OWN source entry. Three records means three sources, not one source with three records' assertions hung off it.

RECORD 1 is an 1850 census, which has no relationship column: NO parent-child or spousal assertion in any form, including inferred ones. Roles may be head_of_household / wife / child_N — those are labels and assert nothing about parentage. Noting the apparent family in the summary is correct practice.

RECORD 2 is a marriage: the parties speak for themselves, so their own facts and the parents' names they stated are informant_proximity 'self'. A stated parent name is record_basis 'stated', never 'inferred' — the record prints it. The witnesses are FAN associates; extract their identifying facts only.

RECORD 3 is a burial register entry that names no informant. That is informant_proximity 'unknown', and an unknown informant means information_quality 'indeterminate' — never 'secondary'. Do not reach for 'unknown' merely because the source is a register or an index.
Should NOT fabricate facts absent from a record — no occupation for Mary Flynn, no birth date for anyone the records do not date.
Should not silently skip a record it finds difficult. If one cannot be extracted, say which and why.
